paras: The expulsion of Black workers from the Raton round house took place in June 1903, when white employees of the Santa Fe railway round house at Raton, New Mexico Territory, drove their Black co-workers off the job with picks and shovels. It followed the killing of a Raton marshal by a Black train porter, and it was reported in a single item in the Santa Fe New Mexican.

The Santa Fe railway kept a round house at Raton, where both white and Black workmen were employed. According to the New Mexican's Raton column, "considerable feeling" arose after Marshal Jones was killed by "the negro porter of one of the Santa Fe trains."

On the day after the killing, the white men of the round house declared that "either they or the negro workmen had to get out." They then "put the matter to a test" and drove the Black workmen away with picks, shovels and similar weapons. The report gives no number of workers on either side, names no one involved, and mentions no injuries.
No report of arrests, of action by the railway, or of the Black workmen's return was found in the coverage.

The only account appeared on June 17, 1903, in the Santa Fe New Mexican, in a column of Raton news that also covered a train toppled by washouts, plans for a Fourth of July celebration and two weddings. The paper headed the column "Race Feeling Was High. White Men Refused to Work With Colored Men at Raton Round House," presented the expulsion as a consequence of the marshal's killing, and offered no comment on the men driven out. No other report of the expulsion was found in either the white or the Black press.

reader.title: Expulsion of Black workers from the Raton round house
bases: White workmen at the Santa Fe railway round house refused to work alongside Black workmen and drove them off the job with picks and shovels (A10).
Only one report, a Raton news column in the Santa Fe New Mexican, describes the round-house expulsion (A10); the wire and territorial reports of the related shooting and jail mob do not mention it.

accounts.label: Raton correspondent, Santa Fe New Mexican
accounts.gist: Feeling over the killing of Marshal Jones by a Black train porter led the white round-house men the next day to declare that they or the Black workmen must go, and they drove the Black workmen away with picks and shovels.

framing.detail: The Santa Fe New Mexican ran the item between notes on rain, a Fourth of July committee and weddings, headed 'Race Feeling Was High', and explained the expulsion by the killing without comment on the workmen driven out.

record_check.dossier: Not dated in the source; 'the following day' after the killing of Marshal Jones. Other reports of the shooting put it about midnight on the night of June 10, so June 11 is plausible but not stated.

No injuries reported (0 reported, not confirmed none)
The Albuquerque Daily Citizen item (A8) is not about the event; the only report is the Santa Fe New Mexican of 1903-06-17, p. 3.
